learningObjective: Reason about executing a single model across heterogeneous devices (CPU + GPU + specialized accelerator) coordinated by a runtime.

canonicalClaims.claim: Heterogeneous execution partitions the graph into device-specific subgraphs with explicit inter-device transfers; the partitioning cost model must account for asymmetric op coverage on accelerators and the transfer/sync cost of cross-device edges.
conditions: The runtime supports pluggable execution providers or backends.
The target machine has multiple distinct devices with distinct op coverage.
nonImplications: Does not imply hardware cache coherence is required.
Does not imply coarsest partition is always best.

misconceptions.claim: Heterogeneous execution requires hardware cache coherence.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Explicit transfers between distinct memory spaces work fine; coherence is convenient but not required.

misconceptions.claim: All devices in a heterogeneous partition support the same ops.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Accelerators typically have restricted op coverage; the partition must handle unsupported ops.

misconceptions.claim: Cross-device transfer cost can be ignored in partitioning.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Transfer + synchronization can dominate fine-grained op savings.

misconceptions.claim: Heterogeneous execution only benefits inference, never training.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Training can also span heterogeneous devices (e.g., CPU offload for optimizer states).
